newsitem.title: USA: Citicorp loses legal round in Lloyd's case.
newsitem.headline: Citicorp loses legal round in Lloyd's case.

text.p: A U.S. court has ruled for plaintiffs in early legal skirmishing in a lawsuit alleging a Citicorp unit mishandled trust funds of the Lloyd's of London insurance market.
On January 24, Judge Robert Sweet of the U.S. District court for the Southern District of New York denied part of Citibank's motion to dismiss the case, allowing it to go forward in New York.
The 65-page written opinion found for Citibank on one of its claims but ruled against Citibank on other claims.

Sweet ruled that the bank could not invoke the so-called forum selection clauses in the contracts between Lloyd's and its investors who are known as "Names." The clauses say that disputes must be litigated in the United Kingdom.

The judge instructed attorneys for the plaintiffs to amend the complaint to include in the definition of a class all Names who underwrote American business. Plaintiffs' attorneys were also told to submit additional facts "related to their request for an injuncton prohibiting Citibank from transferring funds to Lloyd's."

A spokesman for the plaintiffs said that under Sweet's order, the group's complaint will be amended to include in the class definition all Names, including non-U.S. and U.S. citizens, who have participated in Lloyd's American insurance business.

Citicorp spokesman John Morris said the ruling "was in the context of Citibank's motion to dismiss the complaint, which required that he accept all of plaintiffs' allegations as true for the purpose of deciding the motion even though those allegations have not yet been tested, and even though Citibank's side has not been heard."

Citibank served as trustee of the Lloyd's American Trust Fund, which held premiums and other payments made by underwriting Names for insurance policies payable in American dollars. "Citibank has accounted for all of those funds, and is confident that no Name has lost a single dollar because of Citibank's administration of the trust fund," the bank's statement said.
Sweet must still rule on whether to certify it as a class action.
Citicorp has maintained that its actions were scrupulous and that they conformed to the Trust agreement.
About 95 percent of Names worldwide agreed to a plan to reorganize Lloyd's, resinsuring billions of dollars through a new company called Equitas.
